cards.explanation: The answer is the Philistines. The LORD delivered Israel into the hand of the Philistines for forty years (Judges 13:1). Forty YEARS, friends. I thought my stretch in a junk drawer felt long, and I at least had a twist tie in there to talk to.

The answer is that she will conceive and give birth to a son. The angel says, “…you will conceive and give birth to a son.” (Judges 13:3). Picture it, friends. Somebody tells you the hard thing is true, and then in the very same breath says, “But watch this.” That's a good turn in a story.

The answer is that the boy will begin to set Israel free from the Philistines. The angel says the boy “…will begin the deliverance of Israel from the hand of the Philistines.” (Judges 13:5). Notice the word “begin,” friends. He starts the job, and the angel doesn't say he finishes it.

The answer is True. Manoah's wife says, “I did not ask him where he came from, and he did not tell me his name.” (Judges 13:6). She also says his appearance was like the angel of God, “exceedingly awesome.” A visitor that awesome, friends, and no name tag.

The answer is True. When Manoah's wife repeats the message, she tells him about the wine, the strong drink and the unclean food (Judges 13:7). She also says the boy will be a Nazirite to God. But the part about no razor touching his head isn't in her retelling, friends.

The answer is “raise.” Manoah prays, “…let the man of God You sent us come to us again to teach us how to raise the boy who is to be born.” (Judges 13:8). He hasn't even met the baby yet and he's already asking for the lesson. I wish more of us would ask for instructions BEFORE the dough's in the oven, friends.

The answer is False. Judges 13:9 says the angel of God returned to the woman as she was sitting in the field, “but her husband Manoah was not with her.” The same verse says God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel returned. His prayer got answered, friends, and he missed the front-row seat.

The answer is that she runs quickly to tell her husband. “The woman ran quickly to tell her husband…” (Judges 13:10). She doesn't walk it and she doesn't wait. Good news makes people move, friends, and I've seen a lot of bakers run to the oven when it smells right.

The answer is True. Manoah asks, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?” and the man answers, “I am” (Judges 13:11). A short answer, friends, and it's all Manoah needs to hear. I'd say that's a man who knows his facts.

The answer is that his wife must do all the angel told her. The angel of the LORD answers, “Your wife is to do everything I told her.” (Judges 13:13). Then he repeats it in the next verse: “She must do everything I have commanded her.” (Judges 13:14). Manoah asked a big question, friends, and got a plain, clear answer.

The answer is True. The angel says, “She must not eat anything that comes from the vine, nor drink any wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean.” (Judges 13:14). The vine is new in that list, friends, since the first time the angel spoke he mentioned wine, strong drink and unclean food (Judges 13:4). And he ends with, “She must do everything I have commanded her.”

The answer is that they should offer it up instead. The angel says, “Even if I stay, I will not eat your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” (Judges 13:16). So an offering is for the LORD, not for the angel's plate. Manoah wanted to host a guest, friends, and the angel points him to the LORD instead.

The answer is False. The angel of the LORD does not tell Manoah his name. Manoah asks for it, and the angel says, “Why do you ask my name, since it is beyond comprehension?” (Judges 13:18). So Manoah walks away without a name, friends. Honestly, I'd have asked twice.

The answer is “ascended.” “When the flame went up from the altar to the sky, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame.” (Judges 13:20). The text says the LORD did a marvelous thing, and Manoah and his wife looked on as it happened. When they saw it, they fell facedown to the ground. That's a visit nobody forgets, friends.

The answer is True. “When Manoah and his wife saw this, they fell facedown to the ground.” (Judges 13:20). They go down right after the flame goes up and the angel ascends in it. Both of them, friends, and straight down. I've dropped to the floor myself, mostly when I've dropped a whole tray of dough.

The answer is “We are going to die.” Manoah says it to his wife, “…for we have seen God!” (Judges 13:22). I think that came out fast and shaky, friends. That's a man whose heart has just caught up with what his eyes saw.

The answer is that the LORD accepted their offerings. Manoah's wife says, “If the LORD had intended to kill us, He would not have accepted the burnt offering and the grain offering from our hands…” (Judges 13:23). She goes on to say He wouldn't have shown them all these things or spoken to them this way. Manoah brought fear, friends, and I think she brought a calm look at what had actually happened.

The answer is the Spirit of the LORD. “…the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him at Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.” (Judges 13:25). The boy grew, the LORD blessed him, and then the Spirit began to stir. The word “began” tells me something is just getting started, friends.
